findings.where: the fast-tick cluster: stuck_with_me (Mischief), overwhelmed (Static), confetti (Sparkle), catch (Mischief), tangled (Static)
findings.what: Five feelings across four families occupy the same felt box - 400-500 ms long, 5-10 pulses, 12-20 Hz, mean amplitude 195-228 of 255 - and the closest pair, stuck_with_me (30@220 off30 x8: 480 ms, 8 pulses, 16.7 Hz, flat 220) and overwhelmed ((25@255 off25 25@200 off25) x5: 500 ms, 10 pulses, 20 Hz, mean 227.5), differ by 4 per cent in duration, 3 per cent in mean amplitude and 3.3 Hz in rate, with neither carrying an amplitude ramp to tell them apart; on my own 10 ms-grid, 40 ms-integrated, Stevens-weighted waveform distance they sit at 23.8 against a median pairwise distance of 133.5 and a 5th percentile of 52.6.
findings.why: The row requires each of the thirty-plus feelings to be identifiable by its haptic pattern alone with the screen face down; two of these are below any plausible duration and amplitude discrimination threshold and belong to different families, so the confusion is between an affectionate feeling and a distress one. logs/haptics.check.json reports near_shapes: [] and problems: [], which is true of the notation strings (36 distinct) but is not a test of what a finger can separate.

findings.what: Every one of the six notifications the service worker is recorded as showing is kind 'feeling' or kind 'message' - there is no state_declared or state_passive record anywhere, and no widget, lock screen or other closed-app surface in the evidence; 05_settings.png does offer 'something they say about themselves' and 'something their phone notices' set to 'quietly', but nothing in the capture ever fires one, and ambient.held_by_the_phone is [] in all sixteen scene reports.
findings.why: The row requires state changes to be perceptible without opening the app. What is demonstrated with the app closed (app_open: false) is a feeling and a message; the state half of the claim is a setting, not a shown behaviour, and the log's own note says there is no lock screen in evidence and that iOS behaviour is not shown anywhere in this build.

findings.where: the twenty capability rows and the faults injected against them
findings.what: The word 'feeling' occurs once in the whole file (in a search-query string). All twenty checks - send, ack, read, reply, react, edit, delete, typing, voice_note, video, viewer, search, draft_survival, kill_mid_send, offline_queue (26 events), reconnect_ordering, refusal_and_retry, pairing_refused, host_offline_outbox - exercise message, photo, voice and video paths only. coldstart.json crosses one built-in feeling over the tailnet in each direction, but no authored feeling crosses a real link anywhere in the evidence, and nothing tests that an authored feeling's definition (object, sound, waveform) reaches the far phone before a feeling that uses it.
findings.why: The row requires user-authored feelings to behave identically to built-ins in every path. Sending, arrival, family membership, intensity scaling and the shelf are shown for pigeon and soup, but the fault paths - offline queue, kill mid-send, refusal and retry, reconnect ordering - are evidenced for messages and asserted for nothing else, so 'every path' is not measured.

findings.where: the bottom-right corner and the top strip
findings.what: The dog-ear that opens the feeling picker is absent: inside the triangle's usual footprint (y 2868-2945, x 1440-(y-2868)..1440) the mean luma is 93.74 against 96.13 just outside it, a contrast of -2.4, where in the other nine stills it is a constant 195.5 against 93-129 of desk. The pinned standing-line strip is also gone: rows 60-190 mean luma 91.58 here against 219.75 in every other still.
findings.why: The row asks for a feeling reachable in one gesture from any region of the app and for ambient presence surfaces; in the region the app's own report calls 'viewer' there is neither the reach nor the presence line, so one named region has no route to a feeling at all.

findings.where: the dog-ear at the bottom right, y 2868-2945
findings.what: The one-gesture affordance is a flat right triangle with 77-device-pixel legs - about 26 CSS pt a side, roughly 330 pt2, some 17 per cent of the area of a 44x44 pt minimum touch target. Its interior luma standard deviation is 3.34 against 6.44 for the partner note beside it and 12.37 for the wood under it; it has no fold shading, no cast shadow, and no sheet behind it, so it is a triangle lying on bare wood rather than a lifted corner of anything. In 04_moments.png the same triangle sits over a pale sheet at luma 195.65 against 199.18, a contrast of 3.5 grey levels.
findings.why: The gesture is region-independent - 15_authored_feeling.mp4 opens the picker with it from both US and Pulse - but the only thing that advertises it is a mark too small to hit reliably and, on a light ground, effectively invisible, which makes 'reachable in one gesture from any region' true of the code and doubtful of the reader.

findings.where: the whole sheet: 'this one, the iphone', 'add it to the home screen', 'put this phone on the tailnet', 'install the profile the other phone is serving'
findings.what: The iPhone setup names four things and none of them is how a feeling will arrive on a phone that cannot vibrate. 05_settings.png's interrupt sheet offers only 'wake me / quietly / not at all'. The substitute - the whole page moving with the waveform - is never named, described or offered as a setting anywhere a reader can see it.
findings.why: The row asks for a substitute that reads as deliberately designed rather than as a missing feature. The mechanism is designed (see what_is_working), but on the one screen written for the iPhone the app is silent about it, so a reader arriving on iOS is left to discover it or to read the absence of a buzz as an absence.

findings.what: breathe's current waveform is '500@60 700@130 off900 1400@90', total 3500 ms; the sound file shipped for it was composed against '1200@110 off800 1200@110' and is 2500 ms long, with its second press placed at 2000 ms. It is the only one of the thirty-six where the two disagree - the other thirty-five match string for string, and thirty-five of thirty-six sound durations are within 400 ms of the haptic total, median 144 ms - so on this one feeling the page keeps moving for a second after the sound has stopped.
findings.why: The substitute's physicality depends on sound and motion describing the same event; on the longest feeling in the set they describe two different ones.

findings.what: No artifact in the set shows a gesture on one screen and the sensation on another. The reason given is measured rather than asserted - no /dev/kvm, the x86_64 image under QEMU instruction emulation, adbd answering after 113 minutes with no framework behind it, no GTK for a desktop stand-in, and an explicit statement that nothing was faked from the PWA - and WHY_MISSING.json adds that the far phone in 08 is a headless host daemon with no screen by construction. That is a reason, not an excuse. It still leaves the sending half of 'a gesture on one device' evidenced only as a scripted call: 'far feeling hold 0.92' in 08, sendFeeling in 15.
findings.why: The row is written as one device to the other. The receiving end is measured to within a frame; the sending end is a script line and, in 15, a picker tap on the same phone that receives - the arc is never closed in one picture.

findings.where: frames 118-148, the exit of 'hold' on the Pulse region
findings.what: The arriving object recedes toward the shelf - measured against the settled frame 149, its footprint falls from 350,000 px over threshold at frame 110 to 220,000 at 120, 61,000 at 140 and 84 at 148, and its centroid rises from y 1257 to y 902 - but its peak contrast falls with it, 230 to 167 to 104 to 65 to 38 over the last eight frames, so the last 130 ms is a dissolve rather than an arrival at anywhere. Nothing is deposited: the small copy on the shelf is already present in frame 2.
findings.why: The object channel is the weakest of the three. A physical thing does not go transparent, and the shelf entry that would make the recession a landing is written before the animation starts.

findings.where: the three lenses, 'WHAT WE SENT / WHAT HAPPENED / WHAT WE FELT'
findings.what: The report for this frame counts 1340 events under the feelings lens against 183 media and 154 milestones, but the still is shot on the media lens and no artifact in the set shows the feelings lens populated - the largest body of transmitted feeling in the app is never pictured.
findings.why: The row asks for each person's inner state to be continuously legible; a year of 1340 feelings is the surface where that legibility would be strongest and it is the one surface of the three that was not captured.

what_is_working: The non-haptic substitute is the strongest measured thing in this evidence set, and because every clip was shot under WebKit with the app's own record saying channel: 'page' (logs/haptics.json channel_here, and sensation.channel in the 08 and 15 reports), what is on screen IS the substitute rather than a stand-in for it. Tracking whole-page vertical displacement by row-profile alignment against the first frame of each run, the page reproduces each feeling's declared waveform: hold (900@150 off100 900@150, 1900 ms) moves for frames 1-56, falls to -2 px for seven frames, moves again for frames 64-118, measured span 1888 ms; squeeze 624 ms against 640; nuzzle 976 against 990; soup 1184 against 1200; 'here' in 08_state_propagating.mp4 gives three 400 ms bursts with two rests that return to 0 px, 1984 ms against 2000. Every one is exactly one frame short of the declared total, which is my measurement's own quantisation.

The displacement is proportional to the declared amplitude, not decorative. Across the twelve non-silent segments in 07_feeling_landing.mp4 the correlation between segment amplitude and peak page displacement is 0.978 and the fit is px = 0.106 x amp + 0.03 - an intercept of essentially zero. Inside squeeze alone the three segments (90, 160, 230) give 9, 17 and 24 px, a normalised 0.375 : 0.708 : 1.0 against a declared 0.391 : 0.696 : 1.0. During declared silences the page returns to -1 or -2 px, so the gaps are real gaps.

Intensity is a continuous channel that survives the wire. soup sent from the far device at 0.55, 0.7 and 0.9 arrives with base amplitudes scaled to 0.756, 0.838 and 0.947 (logs/08 and logs/15 sensation.pattern) and shakes the page 16, 17 and 19 px peak-to-peak. The sender feels it too: over frames 73-92 of 15_authored_feeling.mp4 the pinned top strip shows pigeon's three 30 ms ticks and their 80 ms gaps as three separate bursts before the picker's layout shift takes over.

A feeling is categorically not a message in another colour, and the evidence proves it by the negative case. In 08_state_propagating.mp4 the arrival of a state change (frames 0-15) and of a message (frames 165-183) produce a whole-page displacement of exactly 0 px, while every feeling arrival in the same clip moves the page 15-22 px on its own waveform. The state change instead lays down a new sheet: frames 0-4 show the partner card physically replaced, MOOD bright becoming restless, and the standing line at the top of every region changes from 'bright ... travelling' to 'restless ... out'.

Thirty-four built-in feelings across six families named on paper tabs in the picker - WARMTH, ACHE, SHELTER, MISCHIEF, STATIC, SPARKLE, legible in frame 8 and frame 70 of 15_authored_feeling.mp4 - against a required thirty across five. All thirty-six carry a distinct object id, a distinct sound id, a distinct name and a distinct waveform string; durations run 30 ms to 3500 ms and pulse counts 1 to 10.

Each feeling has a composed sound, not a beep. assets/sound holds thirty-six feeling files built from fifteen named paper-and-hand primitives (crumple, flick, page_turn, pat, peel, pour, press, punch, rustle, scratch, slide, tap, tear, breath_in, breath_out) placed at millisecond offsets against the waveform; thirty-five of thirty-six durations land within 400 ms of the haptic total, median 144 ms, peaks all between -3.10 and -2.51 dBFS. The clip logs are honest that the audio is the app's own ogg mixed over silence and not a recording of the running app.

Twelve labelled partner-state signals are on the picture, not just in the model: MOOD, HERE, WHERE, NEED, ENERGY, BATTERY, LAST UP, THEIR CLOCK, RINGER, MOVING, SIGNAL, AT HOME on the Pulse card of 01_pulse.png, with the handwritten standing line above them making thirteen. The report carries fourteen, the extra being 'charging', which is false in every scene and so never rendered.

Authored feelings sit in the built-in vocabulary rather than beside it. pigeon (Mischief, noor) appears as the seventh item on the Mischief page of the picker in the same grid, same size, same caption treatment as poke, nyeh, catch, pick one, snap and stuck with me; soup (Shelter, teo) arrives as a modelled orange loop on a card, the same class of object as the candle and the clover. Both scale with intensity, both land on three different regions across 07 and 15, and both are drawn on the same 3500 ms scale as the built-ins in crops/haptics_strip.png.

The arriving object is lit by the scene rather than stamped on it. In 07_feeling_landing.mp4 the candle for 'hold' hovers over the partner note with a soft shadow that tracks it across the paper and off the torn edge onto the wood, and crops/dusk_pulse.png re-renders the same six shelf objects under a low warm key with longer shadows - so the feeling objects are in the room's light, not sprites.

The corner affordance is genuinely region-independent where it exists: identical at luma 195.5 in nine of the ten stills, and 15_authored_feeling.mp4 opens the picker from it over both the US region (frame 8) and the Pulse region (frame 155). 12_search.png carries a FEELINGS filter chip, so the feeling history is searchable alongside the messenger's.

The notification copy is written for a person: 'noor / is holding something out' for a feeling and 'noor / wrote something' for a message, with fourteen words_for_kinds and per-kind interrupt settings phrased as 'something written', 'their voice', 'something they say about themselves'. logs/strings.json reads 116 displayed strings against eight rules - emoji, exclamation marks, product cheer, the reader called a user, the app naming itself, onboarding voice, engagement machinery, streak language - and finds zero.
verdict: Judged where the row asks it to be judged - the landing clip, the propagation clip, and what stands in for the two-device frame - the sensation half of this is real and I could measure it to within a frame. Under WebKit with the app's own record saying the channel is the page, every feeling arrival displaces the whole page on its declared waveform (hold 1888 ms against 1900, squeeze 624 against 640, nuzzle 976 against 990, soup 1184 against 1200, here 1984 against 2000), with displacement proportional to declared amplitude at r = 0.978 and px = 0.106 x amp, silences that return to a pixel of rest, an intensity that survives the wire, a composed paper-and-hand sound per feeling, and a lit object whose shadow tracks it across the sheet - while a message and a state change arriving in the same clip move the page by exactly nothing. That negative case is what makes the claim: a feeling here is not a message in a different colour, it is a different kind of event. Thirty-four built-ins across six named families, twelve labelled partner signals on the picture, and two authored feelings that pick from the same grid and land the same way carry the counts. What holds it to the floor rather than above it is the outer ring. Five feelings across four families sit inside the same 400-500 ms, 12-20 Hz, amplitude-220 box, and the closest pair - stuck with me and overwhelmed - differ by four per cent of duration and three per cent of amplitude with no ramp to separate them, so 'identifiable by its haptic pattern alone with the screen face down' fails for a named cluster, and the check that says otherwise is a test of distinct strings, not of fingers. Nothing in the evidence shows a state change reaching a closed app: the six worker records are all feelings and messages, held_by_the_phone is empty in all sixteen reports, and the three presence surfaces that are actually shown live inside the app. The twenty reliability rows, including every fault path, are messenger paths - the word 'feeling' appears once in that file - so authored parity is demonstrated on the happy path and asserted on the rest. And the gesture that reaches a feeling from any region is a flat 26-point triangle with no fold, no shadow and nothing behind it, invisible against a light sheet and missing altogether from the viewer. Seventeen: the mechanism is built and measured, the enumerated ring around it is not yet.
